spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
## Description

In Iris multi-backend mode, each task backend owns its live worker inventory and
placement (which attempt runs on which worker). The in-process RPC backend keeps
this in a local store, and the design rule is: a backend's worker/placement store
is a **cache**, not durable truth. If a backend loses it, that is treated as "all
tasks were lost" — the controller's durable record (`task X is assigned/running on
backend Y`) re-routes the work through the normal reschedule path — never as a
fatal reconcile error.

The one thing blocking a fully store-free RPC backend is the worker reconcile
protocol. Today `ReconcileRequest.desired` is documented as the *complete expected
set*, and a worker stops any local attempt whose UID is absent from it
(`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/worker/worker.py`, `lib/iris/src/iris/rpc/worker.proto`).
A backend that comes up with an empty placement store would therefore tell every
worker to stop everything before it could re-learn what is running.

Add an observe-before-converge (recovery) path to the worker reconcile protocol so
a freshly-started backend can learn the attempts a worker is running *without*
issuing stops, then re-adopt them. With that, the RPC backend's placement store
becomes a pure cache rebuildable from live worker reports + provider state, and the
backend can run with no durable local DB at all.

This overlaps the multi-backend recovery work (the level-triggered reconcile +
epoch fence, "PR4" of the program); file it so the store-free-backend endpoint is
tracked on its own.

### Definition of Done

- The worker reconcile protocol supports an observe-only / recovery phase: a backend
  learns running attempts from worker reports without those reports being read as a
  desired-set teardown.
- A backend that starts with an empty placement store re-adopts the attempts its
  workers report rather than stopping them.
- The in-process RPC backend can run with an ephemeral (non-durable) placement store.
- Covered by a restart test: wipe the backend's placement store mid-run; running
  attempts survive and are re-adopted.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 This is design-stage, multi-module work (proto change + worker reconcile + backend recovery + ephemeral store + restart test) that **overlaps the in-flight multi-backend "PR4" program** (design #6718; impl #6730, #6731). The RPC backend's placement store referenced in the DoD does not exist on `main` yet — it lands with those PRs. Per the agent scope rule (>100 LOC / multi-module / design), no PR; posting root cause + a proposed approach for a human to review and sequence against PR4.

# Research

The only thing forcing a backend to keep durable placement is the reconcile protocol's *complete-desired-set* semantics. `ReconcileRequest` carries `worker_id` + `desired` and nothing else; the worker treats any non-terminal local attempt whose UID is **absent** from `desired` as a zombie and kills it. A backend that restarts with an empty placement store sends an empty `desired` and tells every worker to stop everything before it can re-learn what is running.

**Relevant code**
- [`worker.proto#L73-L76`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/rpc/worker.proto#L73-L76) — `ReconcileRequest`, `desired` = "complete expected set"
- [`worker.py#L871-L881`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/worker/worker.py#L871-L881) — zombie-kill: absent-from-`desired` ⇒ `_kill_async`
- [`worker.py#L889-L911`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/worker/worker.py#L889-L911) — observations bounded to `desired` ∪ zombies (won't surface unknown-to-backend attempts)
- [`reconcile/worker.py#L110-L221`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/worker.py#L110-L221) — `build_reconcile_plans` builds `desired` from durable state
- [`controller/backend.py#L340-L363`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/backend.py#L340) — `TaskBackend` protocol (where the RPC backend + its placement store hangs)

The existing worker-side container adoption ([`worker.py#L319-L398`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/worker/worker.py#L319-L398)) recovers attempts across a *worker* restart; this issue is the symmetric case for a *backend* restart, and needs a protocol affordance rather than local container scanning.

# Proposed Approach

**1. Add an observe-only phase to the reconcile protocol.** Add a field to `ReconcileRequest` — `bool observe_only = 3;` (or a `ReconcileMode mode` enum if more phases are foreseen). When set, the worker:
  - skips the zombie-kill loop ([`worker.py#L871-L881`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/worker/worker.py#L871-L881)) — absence is *not* a stop signal;
  - still applies explicit `run`/`stop` intents (so a recovering backend can keep handing out specs);
  - reports its **complete** non-terminal attempt set in `observed`, not just the desired∩local subset ([`worker.py#L889-L911`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/worker/worker.py#L889-L911)).

This makes the absent-UID case mean "I don't know yet," distinct from today's "stop this."

**2. Backend recovery (observe → adopt → converge).** A backend that comes up with an empty placement store runs an observe-only sweep across its workers, rebuilds placement from `observed` attempt UIDs cross-referenced with the controller's durable `task assigned/running on backend Y` record (and provider state), then flips to normal converge mode. Attempts the durable record disowns fall out through the existing reschedule path — never a fatal reconcile error.

**3. Ephemeral placement store.** Once placement is rebuildable from live worker reports + provider state, the in-process RPC backend's store becomes a pure cache and can be non-durable. This piece lands against the RPC backend introduced in #6730/#6731.

**4. Test.** Restart test: with attempts running, wipe the backend's placement store mid-run; assert running attempts are observed and re-adopted (not stopped) and that no `stop`/zombie-kill is issued during the observe phase. A focused worker-level test (`tests/cluster/worker/test_reconcile.py`) can assert that an `observe_only` reconcile with empty `desired` returns the full observed set and kills nothing.

**Sequencing question for a human:** steps 1–2 (protocol + worker semantics) are independent of the RPC-backend store and could land first as a small, self-contained proto+worker change with the worker-level test. Steps 3–4 should ride on PR4 (#6730/#6731) where the store exists. Recommend splitting along that line unless PR4 owners want it bundled.

spillover_issues.author: teetone
spillover_issues.body:
Goal: Investigate whether Self-Verified Distillation improves post-trained Marin checkpoints

Self-Verified Distillation generates candidate solutions from a post-trained model, filters them using verification, and trains on the accepted self-curated data. The goal of this issue is to evaluate whether this procedure further improves a post-trained Marin checkpoint using unlabeled seed questions. The original SVD paper studies this setting without external teachers or tool feedback, where the model generates candidate solutions, self-verifies them, and trains on the resulting filtered dataset.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26132

### Motivation

We want to test whether large post-trained Marin models can further self-improve through on-policy SVD. In the pure setting, the Marin checkpoint is used both as the generator and verifier.

A key risk is that the initial Marin checkpoint may be too weak, as either:

- a generator: producing too few high-quality candidate solutions
- a verifier: failing to reliably distinguish correct from incorrect generations

If self-verification is the bottleneck, we should also evaluate a variant that keeps Marin on-policy generation but uses a stronger verifier for filtering.

## Goal

Honest replication of the paper's base-size experiment (Table 6) with a dense model: d8 (width 1024, ~210M params, vocab 50,304), 1B tokens of FineWeb with the GPT-2 tokenizer, batch 524,288, 2048-token sequences, under the paper's own Table 5 hyperparameters.

Three arms (branch `paper-replication`, variant `experiments/grug/paper_rep/`):

| Arm | Model | Recipe | Paper target (val loss) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vanilla` | plain transformer | Vanilla | 3.3279 |
| `op1` | Operator-1 (K=1, 2/3/3 split, alpha 1) | Operator-1 | 3.3057 |
| `op1-vanilla-recipe` | Operator-1 | Vanilla | 3.3135 |

The third arm is the paper's recipe-transfer probe. The replication succeeds if the ordering and approximate gaps match (Operator-1 own < Operator-1 vanilla-recipe < Vanilla, gaps about -0.022 / -0.014).

- Variant PR: (added below)

- Documented deviations (WD placement, Muon internals, FineWeb 10BT slice, sequence packing) are listed in the variant README.

- [ ] Materialize FineWeb caches (one-time download + tokenize)
